title: Save a link under your title
description: Save a link with a title you wrote, not only the title the page gave you.
oneStarDescription: Write a title that says why you saved it.
twoStarDescription: Save the address with that title.
threeStarDescription: Find the link from your title later the same day.

title: Say the assumption aloud
description: Say the assumption the plan depends on, and ask if it is still true.
oneStarDescription: Write the one assumption in a sentence.
twoStarDescription: Ask the other person if it is still true.
threeStarDescription: Write what you will change if it is not true.

title: Say when a number is rounded
description: Say whether a printed number is a count you could check or a round figure.
oneStarDescription: Write the number and the unit beside it.
twoStarDescription: Label it as a count, a round figure, or unknown, and point to the word that tells you.
threeStarDescription: Write one comparison you will not make until you know how it was rounded.

title: Say who a memorial speaks to
description: Read a short memorial and say who it addresses.
oneStarDescription: Read the words that are actually there.
twoStarDescription: Say who the words speak to, from the words themselves.
threeStarDescription: Write one group or event the text does not mention.

title: See which way a spinner turns
description: Launch a simple spinner twice, once with each hand direction, and say which way it turned.
oneStarDescription: Spin it and say the direction you saw.
twoStarDescription: Change how you start it and say the new direction.
threeStarDescription: Write the start and the turn beside each other.

title: Separate a memory from a paper
description: Write one thing a person remembers and one thing a paper shows about the same event.
oneStarDescription: Write the remembered point in their words if you can.
twoStarDescription: Write one fact the paper shows.
threeStarDescription: Label which is which, and do not merge them into one sentence.

title: Separate an ad from the report
description: Point to the part of a page that is selling something and the part that is reporting.
oneStarDescription: Point to one phrase or picture that asks you to buy, book, or sign up.
twoStarDescription: Point to one sentence that tells what happened, and keep it separate from the pitch.
threeStarDescription: Write one fact you would need before treating the page as a report.

title: Separate the fact you both see
description: Write one fact you can both point to, separate from what each of you prefers.
oneStarDescription: Write a fact both of you can see or reread.
twoStarDescription: Write each preference on a different line.
threeStarDescription: Ask them to correct the fact before you discuss the preference.

title: Set a lost-and-found spot
description: Put one labeled spot for lost items and tell the group where it is.
oneStarDescription: Pick a spot people can see.
twoStarDescription: Label it so a stranger can tell what it is for.
threeStarDescription: Say or write the location before the event is underway.

title: Set a sample before the batch
description: Make or show one sample and get a yes before you make the rest.
oneStarDescription: Finish one sample of the ordinary thing.
twoStarDescription: Ask the other person if that sample is the one to repeat.
threeStarDescription: Make the rest only after a yes, or stop.

title: Set a scene with three objects
description: Place three objects and say what happened in the moment just before.
oneStarDescription: Place three objects where someone else can see them.
twoStarDescription: Tell what happened just before, using those objects.
threeStarDescription: Ask the other person for the next moment, using the same objects.

title: Sew a short hem
description: Sew a short hem on scrap cloth with stitches you can point to.
oneStarDescription: Fold the edge and hold it.
twoStarDescription: Sew a short length with stitches you can see.
threeStarDescription: Point to one stitch and say what it holds.

title: Shoot from two heights
description: Take two photos of one object, one higher and one lower, and say what each shows.
oneStarDescription: Take one photo from above and say what you can see.
twoStarDescription: Take one photo from lower down and say what appeared.
threeStarDescription: Label each photo with the height so a viewer can tell them apart.

title: Show every step of one example
description: Write one worked example with every step visible, including the last result.
oneStarDescription: Choose a task of a few steps you can finish.
twoStarDescription: Write each step so a reader can see it.
threeStarDescription: Ask someone which step they had to guess, and add that step.

title: Show the line that fixes a step
description: Show one wrong step and the line that fixes it.
oneStarDescription: Write a step with one clear error.
twoStarDescription: Write the corrected line beside it.
threeStarDescription: Cover the labels and ask someone to pick the fix.

title: Show what you carried out
description: Show that what you carried out of a place matches what you brought in, plus any litter you meant to remove.
oneStarDescription: List what is in the bag at the start.
twoStarDescription: List it again at the end.
threeStarDescription: Explain any item that was added or used.

title: Show what you moved
description: Photograph or list a setting before you change it, then show what you moved.
oneStarDescription: Make a photo or a list before the change.
twoStarDescription: Move one thing and leave the rest where it was.
threeStarDescription: Show the before and after and name the thing you moved.

title: Sit where they can see you
description: Sit where the person you are with can see your face without turning sharply.
oneStarDescription: Ask where they would like you to sit.
twoStarDescription: Sit there, or explain the one seat you cannot use.
threeStarDescription: Ask if they can see you well enough to talk.

title: Sketch posture without naming a species
description: Sketch a bird or animal's posture and write that you are not naming the species.
oneStarDescription: Draw the posture you see, not a field-guide copy.
twoStarDescription: Write that the sketch is not an identification.
threeStarDescription: Add one clue you saw, labeled as a clue rather than a name.

title: Slide a block on two surfaces
description: Slide the same small block on two surfaces and say which one stopped sooner.
oneStarDescription: Name the two surfaces before you start.
twoStarDescription: Use a similar start and mark where the block stops.
threeStarDescription: Wipe one surface and say whether the stop changed.

title: Sort screws by the head you can see
description: Sort a small mix of screws by the head you can see, into labeled cups.
oneStarDescription: Label cups with the head shapes you actually have.
twoStarDescription: Put each screw in the cup that matches its head.
threeStarDescription: Put one unclear screw aside instead of forcing it.

title: Stack the talking piece
description: Use one object as a talking piece and pass it before the next person speaks.
oneStarDescription: Put one object in the middle and say what it means.
twoStarDescription: Speak only while you hold it, once.
threeStarDescription: Hand it to the next person and stop.

title: Start from a sound
description: Start a one-minute story from a sound you just heard, and name the sound.
oneStarDescription: Write the sound you are using.
twoStarDescription: Tell one minute that begins with that sound.
threeStarDescription: At the end, point to the moment the sound mattered.

title: Stitch a pamphlet so it opens
description: Stitch a few sheets into a pamphlet that opens and stays together.
oneStarDescription: Fold the sheets together.
twoStarDescription: Sew through the fold so the pages hold.
threeStarDescription: Open the pamphlet and show a page turning without falling out.

title: Stop a joke that leaves someone out
description: Stop a joke you were telling when you see it leaves someone out.
oneStarDescription: Stop the joke before the ending.
twoStarDescription: Say you are stopping because it leaves someone out.
threeStarDescription: Move to a subject that includes the person.

title: Stop after two options
description: Offer two times or two choices, then stop talking.
oneStarDescription: Name two real options and no third one.
twoStarDescription: Do not add a third while they are choosing.
threeStarDescription: Write the one they chose, or that they chose neither.

title: Stop at the turn
description: Tell a short story and stop when it turns, then ask what the listener expects.
oneStarDescription: Mark the moment the situation changes.
twoStarDescription: Read or tell up to that moment and stop.
threeStarDescription: Ask what they expect next, then tell the rest and say what differed.

title: Stop when the question is answered
description: Stop a piece of work when the result answers the question you wrote down.
oneStarDescription: Write the question before you continue.
twoStarDescription: Point to the part of the result that answers it.
threeStarDescription: Stop adding, and write what you did not add.

title: Stop your own sentence
description: Stop your sentence when someone else starts, and let them finish.
oneStarDescription: Stop when their voice starts.
twoStarDescription: Do not restart until they have finished the point.
threeStarDescription: Ask if they want your point, or drop it.

title: Stretch a band and listen
description: Stretch a rubber band and say how the sound changed when you plucked it.
oneStarDescription: Pluck it once while it is loose and describe the sound.
twoStarDescription: Stretch it farther and say what changed in the sound.
threeStarDescription: Let it slack again and say whether the first sound returned.

title: Swap two events
description: Tell two events in the other order and say what the listener now believes.
oneStarDescription: Tell two events in the order they happened.
twoStarDescription: Tell the same facts in the other order.
threeStarDescription: Ask what the listener now thinks caused what, and write their answer.

title: Take an offer and add a fact
description: In a made-up scene, accept what the other person just said and add one new fact.
oneStarDescription: Repeat their fact in your next line without cancelling it.
twoStarDescription: Add one new fact that fits, and stop there.
threeStarDescription: When they respond, do not drop the fact you added.

title: Tap two lids
description: Tap two lids and say which one rings longer.
oneStarDescription: Tap one lid and listen until the sound dies.
twoStarDescription: Tap the other lid the same way and say which lasted longer.
threeStarDescription: Hold one lid in a different place and say how the sound changed.

title: Teach with the object in their hands
description: Teach one step while the object is in the learner's hands, not yours.
oneStarDescription: Give them the object before you explain.
twoStarDescription: Guide one step with words while they hold it.
threeStarDescription: Let them finish that step and say what you were about to grab.

title: Tell a preview from a review
description: Say whether a short text is selling a future showing or responding to a work the writer saw.
oneStarDescription: Point to a word that places the work in the future or in the past.
twoStarDescription: Point to one detail that could only come from seeing it, or write that there is none.
threeStarDescription: Label it preview or review, and write the clue you used.

title: Test a caption against the picture
description: Say one thing a caption claims that the picture shows, and one thing it does not show.
oneStarDescription: Write the caption's main claim in your words.
twoStarDescription: Point to the part of the picture that supports the claim, or write that you cannot find it.
threeStarDescription: Write one thing a viewer still cannot know from the picture alone.

title: Test glue on a scrap
description: Test a glue on a scrap of the same material before you use it on the real piece.
oneStarDescription: Use a scrap of the same material.
twoStarDescription: Glue the scrap and wait as the container says, or stop if it gives no time.
threeStarDescription: Try to separate the scrap and say whether you will use that glue on the real piece.

title: Tick borrowed things back
description: List items the group borrowed and tick each one when it is back.
oneStarDescription: Write each borrowed item and its owner.
twoStarDescription: Tick an item only when you see it returned.
threeStarDescription: At the end, name any item still out and who has it.

title: Tie a luggage label that stays
description: Tie a label to a bag so it stays on when you lift the bag.
oneStarDescription: Write a name or a code you are willing to show.
twoStarDescription: Tie the label to a handle so it can be lifted.
threeStarDescription: Lift the bag once and show the label stayed.

title: Time two spinners
description: Make two paper spinners, change one thing, and say which spun longer.
oneStarDescription: Make two spinners that match.
twoStarDescription: Change the wing, the clip, or the drop on one spinner only.
threeStarDescription: Drop them from the same height and say which spun longer.
